A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FRUGAL and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Content can be reliably matched despite substantial reformatting, reorganization, additions, and removals.

before.justification: v1 reports original C4 pre-training, GLUE fine-tuning, ablation, and quadratic optimization results, including Tables 2–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments including 3B pre-training, LLaMA-3.1-8B commonsense fine-tuning, and concurrent-optimizer comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the gradient splitting, complementary updates, and optimizer-state management procedures. Blockwise pre-training and columnwise fine-tuning already appear in v1. Lion experiments instantiate the existing configurable framework; the added pseudocode does not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: v2 retains C4 and GLUE and adds Commonsense170K training with evaluation on BoolQ, PIQA, SIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, and OBQA (Section 7.2, Table 7). This substantially extends fine-tuning coverage to decoder-language-model commonsense reasoning.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with AdaMeM, Fira, and LDAdam (Tables 20–21), Lion and GaLore with Lion (Table 11), and a full-parameter GLUE reference row (Table 6). Removing v1's 7B experiment also removes its comparisons with 8-bit Adam and 8-bit GaLore. Adam/AdamW relabeling is not counted as a new comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds 3B training for 300k steps with weight decay and clipping, rank-32 commonsense fine-tuning, GPT-2 tokenization, and precision/model-size controls. Its Fira/LDAdam comparison enables decay and clipping or norm limiting, unlike the retained main C4 protocol. The 20k-step standalone SGD/signSGD experiment becomes a 200k-step FRUGAL comparison, while v1's pure-bfloat16 7B protocol is removed.

E4.justification: New analyses test precision versus model size, GPT-2 architecture, beta2 = 0.95, and Lion as the state-full optimizer. v1's standalone SGD/signSGD learning-rate sweep is replaced by a comparison of those optimizers within FRUGAL (v2 Table 10). Existing scheduler, density, block-selection, update-frequency, output-head, and state-reprojection analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Section 6.3 explicitly reports a single training run for the new 3B experiment because of computational constraints. The existing three-run GLUE mean/standard-deviation reporting and five-run quadratic experiment remain unchanged. Neither version establishes increased repetition for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Retained primary C4/GLUE values remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results. Table 7 reports commonsense averages of 84.89/84.94 for FRUGAL ranks 32/0, versus 84.65 for GaLore and 84.18 for LoRA. Under Table 21's modified protocol, 350M perplexities are 13.99 for FRUGAL, 13.74 for Fira, and 13.54 for LDAdam; these are new comparisons, not same-setting changes from v1. v1's 7B results, standalone optimizer sweep, and Table 1's 20k/100k columns are removed.

T1.justification: v2 Section 5.1 explicitly requires continuous differentiability and Lipschitz gradients, beyond v1's explicit one-sided quadratic-upper-bound definition in Appendix E. This refines the formal smoothness requirements. The convergence rates, appendix proofs, and memory derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions: full-rank gradient splitting, SGDM/SGD convergence guarantees, effective memory-efficient language-model training, and output-layer sensitivity. v1 already claims success with the same or smaller memory budget, so v2's emphasis on less memory does not introduce a substantively new core claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications about hyperparameter tuning, iteration-based versus wall-clock comparisons, untested 7B-plus pre-training, language-only applicability, and potentially better subspace-selection strategies (Appendices B and F). It also interprets new precision experiments as showing that larger bfloat16 models can fail to compensate for precision-related degradation. These substantially expand v1's interpretations and limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds PyTorch-like Algorithms 4–5 documenting projected/block updates and Adam/signSGD internals, plus settings for the new experiments. The code pointer changes from GitHub to an anonymous hosting address, and the removed 7B setup details disappear. The new documentation has a concrete inconsistency: Algorithm 4, line 11 uses grad_full instead of grad in the residual calculation, conflicting with Algorithm 1.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix B substantially revise positioning through detailed comparisons with Fira, LDAdam, and AdaMeM, including residual handling, state reprojection, preconditioning, and computational tradeoffs. AdaMeM is positioned as a special case of FRUGAL. Additional experimental references and removal of some earlier PEFT/coordinate-descent citations accompany this expansion.

P1.justification: Existing introductory and methodological prose is extensively condensed and reorganized. Empirical motivation and the framework become separate sections, pre-training and fine-tuning become separate major sections, and zero-density training receives its own subsection. Appendix organization, terminology such as Logits/Output layer, and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column ICML layout. The three original figures retain their graphics but are resized or relocated. Table 1 is restructured around projection type and residual updating, numerous tables are added or rearranged, and two substantial pseudocode displays are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through decoder-LLM fine-tuning, targeted optimizer and architecture ablations, and comparisons with closely related full-gradient methods, addressing important gaps in v1. Appendix B reports unfavorable comparisons and tuning caveats, while Appendix F clarifies applicability limits. These gains outweigh the removal of preliminary 7B pre-training evidence, although the blanket superiority claim and the inconsistent residual calculation in the new pseudocode remain weaknesses.
